schema_notes: FurnitureLAB catalogue. Each entry: an in-room object (non-electrical, non-signal-bearing) that contributes equivalent absorption area A_obj into the room's Sabine/Eyring/ray-trace physics. Schema authored by Lin (docs-writer, catalogue sub-hat) and reviewed by Dr. Chen against ISO 354 measurement discipline. Reliability tag is non-negotiable: 'measured' (cited ISO 354 lab or peer-reviewed lab), 'derived' (calculated from a parent A_obj or surface-area×alpha mapping with a documented derivation), 'estimated' (engineering judgement; UI badges amber, report flags 'low-confidence'). citation.estimated mirrors reliability for serializer convenience. Schema v2 (2026-05-26): adds short_name (compact 2D / HUD label) and visual.family (3D + iso-glyph dispatch key, one of 'seat' | 'slab-on-legs' | 'vertical-box' | 'flat-pad'); both required on every row. Schema v3 (2026-05-27): adds acoustics.interaction_mode ('porous' | 'reflective') — controls how the precision ray-tracer handles the object. 'porous' items are treated as Beer-Lambert volumetric absorbers (chairs, sofas, drapes, audience blocks — sound diffuses through the upholstery with energy loss per Kuttruff §4.1). 'reflective' items are triangulated into the wall BVH (tables, lecterns, bookshelves, server racks — sound bounces off the hard outer surface). Both contribute A_obj to Sabine/Eyring identically via the rt60 parallel-A sum (Kuttruff §5.3); the mode only changes how rays interact with the object in the precision engine.

items.name: Theater seat, upholstered (occupied)

citation.reference: Beranek L L, Hidaka T. Acoustical absorption by audiences and seats. JASA 104(6) 3169-3177. Per-seat A_obj derived from area-based alpha (medium upholstered audience, occupied) times nominal seat footprint 0.275 m^2.
citation.measurement_method: ISO 354 reverberation-room (source publication); per-seat A_obj is a derivation, not a direct measurement.
citation.notes: Per-seat A_obj derived from Beranek & Hidaka 1998 per-m² α × 0.275 m² seat footprint (Sabine convention). The paper publishes audience-plan α, not per-seat A_obj; Carmen market-research audit 2026-05-27 confirmed no open-access per-seat tabulation exists. Numbers internally consistent with the published α curve.

items.revised_note: Citation honesty pass — clarified derivation method.

citation.reference: Beranek L L, Hidaka T. Acoustical absorption by audiences and seats. JASA 104(6) 3169-3177. Per-seat A_obj derived from area-based alpha for medium upholstered audience, UNOCCUPIED, times nominal seat footprint 0.275 m^2. Empty/occupied differ by ~3x at mids per Beranek 2e Table 7.1 vs 7.2.
citation.measurement_method: ISO 354 reverberation-room (source publication); per-seat A_obj is a derivation, not a direct measurement.
citation.notes: Per-seat A_obj derived from Beranek & Hidaka 1998 per-m² α × 0.275 m² seat footprint for UNOCCUPIED case. Same derivation-vs-direct-measurement caveat as the occupied pair-row. Empty/occupied ratio cross-checks against Beranek 2e Table 7.1 vs 7.2 (~3× at mids).

items.name: Audience block (occupied, per m²)

citation.reference: Beranek L L, Hidaka T. Acoustical absorption by audiences and seats. JASA 104(6) 3169-3177 (1998), Table II — medium-upholstered, fully occupied. PTB / AcousticSphere reproduction confirms these per-m² α values.
citation.measurement_method: ISO 354 reverberation-room (source publication aggregates multiple concert-hall measurements).
citation.notes: Direct cite from Beranek & Hidaka 1998 Table II (medium-upholstered occupied audience). PTB / AcousticSphere reproduces these values from the JASA paper. Use this row when seats are >50 deep; for individual seats use theater-seat-upholstered-occupied instead.

items.revised_note: Upgraded derived → measured. Replaced values with PTB/JASA-cited set ({0.62, 0.72, 0.80, 0.83, 0.84, 0.85}); previous values {0.55, 0.75, 0.85, 0.92, 0.88, 0.85} were from Beranek 2e Table 7.3 (book reproduction with rounding + hall-type weighting). New set is closer to the original 1998 JASA paper.

citation.reference: Bistafa S R, Bradley J S. Reverberation time and maximum background-noise level for classrooms. JASA 108(4) 1721-1731 (2000), Table 2 — student desk + occupant. Adapted here for a generic padded office chair occupied by an adult.
citation.notes: Numbers calibrated against Bistafa & Bradley 2000 classroom reverberation predictions; per-chair Table 2 values not available in open-access form (paper paywalled, ResearchGate copy 403). Plausible curve shape vs. independent "person seated on hard chair" references (aural-exchange compilation 0.33/0.40/0.44/0.45/0.45/0.45) — our values run hotter at mids, suggesting we calibrated to a thicker pad. Phase 1.5: substitute direct numbers if Table 2 becomes accessible.

citation.reference: Bistafa S R, Bradley J S. Reverberation time and maximum background-noise level for classrooms. JASA 108(4) 1721-1731 (2000), Table 2 — student chair unoccupied. Adapted here for a generic padded office chair empty.
citation.notes: Pair-state companion. Same Bistafa & Bradley source caveat as the occupied row — Table 2 not openly published. Empty-chair α ratio relative to occupied calibrated to ~3× per Bistafa & Bradley's methodology.

citation.reference: Cox T J, D'Antonio P. Acoustic Absorbers and Diffusers, 2nd ed. (2009), §3.6 — wood-on-frame office furniture is essentially specular at LF, with mild edge-scattering rising at HF. A_obj = footprint area (2.4 m²) × estimated alpha {0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10}.
citation.measurement_method: Not directly measured; derived from material-class behaviour.
citation.notes: Tables are near-inert acoustically — placing one barely moves RT60. Included for visual completeness and so the BoM reports the right object count, not because it changes the room sound.

citation.reference: No published ISO 354 row for free-standing lecterns. A_obj derived from footprint area (0.27 m²) × wood-finish alpha {0.07, 0.08, 0.08, 0.11, 0.15, 0.19} per Cox & D'Antonio §3.6 generic wood values.
citation.measurement_method: Not directly measured; back-of-envelope derivation from material alpha and footprint.
citation.notes: Acoustically negligible. Placed lecterns won't move RT60. Tagged estimated; if you have a measured lectern row from a vendor cert, swap in and bump reliability.

items.name: Bookshelf, loaded, 1 m wide × 2 m tall

citation.reference: Cox T J, D'Antonio P. Acoustic Absorbers and Diffusers, 2nd ed. (2009), §3.6 irregular-surface absorbers + §6 scattering data. A_obj = face area (1 m × 2 m = 2 m²) × loaded-bookshelf alpha {0.30, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.65}. Scattering coefficients estimated from §6.4 generic irregular-surface envelope.
citation.measurement_method: Not directly measured; alpha derived from material-class measurements.
citation.notes: Loaded bookshelves are surprisingly effective mid/HF absorbers AND diffusers (mix of book covers, depths, spines breaks specular reflection). Both alpha and scattering are populated here; the precision ray tracer (Phase 2) will consume the scattering. Sabine + Eyring only read alpha.

items.name: Prayer mat, unrolled (per m²)

citation.reference: Extrapolated from Beranek "Concert Halls and Opera Houses" 2nd ed. (2004), Table 6.2, "Carpet, thin, over thin felt on concrete" baseline = {0.10, 0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.30, 0.30}. Prayer mat is thinner than the cataloged carpet+felt, so all bands scaled DOWN (~50-80%) from the Beranek baseline. Prior catalogue values (4 kHz 0.45) were too HF-bright — exceeded even thick-pile carpet on sponge.
citation.notes: Carpet absorption rises monotonically with frequency. Prior values had 4 kHz = 0.45 which is implausible for a single thin layer over a hard floor — flagged by Carmen 2026-05-27 citation audit. New curve: {0.05, 0.08, 0.12, 0.18, 0.22, 0.25} — sub-Beranek-thin-carpet shape, mat-realistic.

items.revised_note: Corrected curve shape — 4 kHz reduced 0.45 → 0.25 (was implausibly bright); other bands rescaled to a coherent thin-mat curve. Reliability stays "derived" (extrapolation, not direct measurement).

citation.reference: Estimated from perforated-panel absorber data (Beranek 2e Table 6.8 — perforated steel over absorptive cavity) scaled to a 42U cabinet with ~63% open front door. Cavity-tuned mid-frequency peak typical of perforated absorbers.
